 Former UConn stars Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd announce that they broke up 
 The two shared the news on Friday on Fudd's podcast, Fudd Around And Find Out, revealing that they actually broke up more than a year ago. 
 By Jennifer Lambert • 
 Published November 6, 2026 • 
 Updated on November 6, 2026 at 3:25 pm 
 BOOKMARKER 
 Steph Chambers/Getty Images 
 Former UConn women's basketball stars Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd have announced that they are no longer a couple.
 The two shared the news on Friday afternoon on Fudd's podcast, Fudd Around And Find Out, revealing that they actually broke up more than a year ago.

 "Paige and I have something that we want to share with everyone. We are no longer together," Fudd said while laughing. "I don't know how else to say that."
 Bueckers explained that the breakup happened well before Fudd was drafted to the Dallas Wings, addressing speculation about how their relationship could affect their careers as teammates.
 "We were not together before she got drafted, so all of those narratives can go to bed," Bueckers said.
 Bueckers also made it clear that Fudd's basketball accomplishments had nothing to do with their relationship.

 "She was not drafted because she was my girlfriend," Bueckers said. "She was drafted because she deserved it and she's an amazing human, an amazing basketball player."
 Despite the breakup, the former Huskies said they remain close friends.
 "We broke up over a year ago, so we played an entire season together," Bueckers said. "We're the utmost professional. We care about basketball, and we're still friends, we're still cool."
 View this post on Instagram 
 The two also addressed negativity and speculation surrounding their relationship, emphasizing that they do not support fans tearing either of them down.
 "We don't stand for hate of any kind, like any putting people down to lift us individually, together," Bueckers said. "Any negative nature of that kind, we don't associate with that, we don't condone that."
 Bueckers said they plan to continue supporting each other as friends and teammates while eventually moving on with their personal lives.
 "We are still gonna have other friends; we will eventually move on," Bueckers said. "I know we will continue to be outside and be lit and have a good time."
 "And we don't need messages of what the other person is doing," Fudd said.
 While acknowledging that fans may have more questions, Fudd said the two do not plan to share additional details about their breakup.
 "We know you guys are curious and have a ton of questions, but we've addressed everything we need to and the rest will stay with us," she said.
 The pair ended the announcement on a lighthearted note, making a heart gesture before breaking it apart and joking, "But we're still gang though."
